title: A Second Brain Your AI Agent Can Read: Obsidian + Claude

content_html:
Background

There are so many details we need to remember in life. Recently I've been
working on a legacy project that was written years ago with no maintainers left.
I've had to continuously dig through thousands of lines of my own notes just to
remember how a particular piece of the application works. Sifting through notes
to find one detail takes time I'd rather spend architecting and building.

AI agents change that. They make it much easier to store and retrieve
information you wrote down days, months, or years ago.

What is Obsidian

Obsidian is a note-taking app that stores everything as
plain markdown files. It lets you organize and structure your notes in a
flexible way, and because the files are plain text on disk, anything that can
read a directory can read your notes, including an AI agent.

For projects, I use Obsidian as my personal documentation: how a system works,
why a decision was made, what the process flows are. Think of it as a second
brain. Everything lives in one place.

The part that makes it work with an agent isn't the app, it's the linking.
Obsidian lets you create bidirectional links between notes with
[[Note Name]]. That turns your vault from a pile of files into a graph you can
hand an agent a single entry point to.

How I structure my files

Obsidian is flexible enough that there are a dozen reasonable ways to set this
up. Here's mine, but you can adapt it to whatever fits your style.

I keep two folders. MOC stands for Map of Content, and holds one file per
topic named <Topic Name> - MOC. Permanent Notes holds everything else. Every
time I create a note related to a topic, I link it in both directions:
[[<Permanent note name>]] in the MOC, and [[<Topic Name> - MOC]] in the
note.

The following files are examples:

vault/
├── MOC/
│   └── Legacy Payments API - MOC.md
└── Permanent Notes/
    ├── Payments API - Endpoints.md
    ├── Payments API - Webhook Retry Logic.md
    ├── Payments API - Settlement Flow.md
    └── Payments API - Architecture Decisions.md

And the MOC itself stays deliberately thin:

# Legacy Payments API - MOC

Legacy service handling card settlement.

## Reference

- [[Payments API - Endpoints]]
- [[Payments API - Webhook Retry Logic]]

## Design

- [[Payments API - Settlement Flow]]
- [[Payments API - Architecture Decisions]]

This is the whole trick. Instead of pointing an agent at a folder and hoping it
reads the right things, you point it at one file that tells it exactly which
notes matter and how they relate. You control the context window instead of
letting the file system decide it for you.

Connecting your agent to the vault

There's no plugin or integration to set up here. Because Obsidian notes are just
markdown files on disk, any agent that can read your file system can read your
vault.

My workflow is simple: I open Claude at the vault root and tell it to read a
specific MOC file.

Read MOC/Legacy Payments API - MOC.md and the notes it links to.

Or paste the full path in directly if you'd rather not think about where you
launched from.

The reason to open at the root rather than inside MOC/ is that the links point
outward. Your MOC lives in one folder and every note it references lives in
another, so an agent scoped to MOC/ has to reach outside its working directory
to follow them. Depending on your setup that means approving access every time.

Using an agent with the MOC

When I start researching a topic, I create the MOC first and give the agent the
path to it.

On the legacy project, that meant creating Legacy Payments API - MOC, then
working through the codebase asking Claude to document the API endpoints, the
business logic, and the process flows — with each one landing as its own
permanent note and each one linked back to the MOC. I wrote my architecture
documents into the vault too, so I can reference them later instead of
reconstructing the reasoning from scratch.

Once the MOC has some substance, it becomes the entry point for everything else.
When I need a plan for a new feature, the prompt is roughly:

Read MOC/Legacy Payments API - MOC.md and every note it links to. Then write
an implementation plan for adding partial refunds to the settlement flow. Flag
anything in the existing notes that contradicts the change.

Tips to work efficiently

Two things went wrong for me before this settled into something useful.

Agents write far too much. Ask for documentation on a service and you'll get
a small book. It becomes too dense for a human to actually read. The more text
the agent has to go through, the more likely it is to hallucinate something that
isn't in there.

The fix is the most important habit when working with AI agents: proofread what
the agent wrote before you save it. It's tempting to trust Claude to write notes
and then never look at them, but a proofreading pass lets you cut the sections
you'll never need. Every paragraph you delete now is context the agent doesn't
have to process later.

Notes drift out of sync. New information surfaces in conversation and never
makes it into the vault, so the next time you read the note it's wrong. Keeping
notes short is what makes them maintainable. If you can scan the section headers
of a note in ten seconds, you'll actually update it. Long notes are far less
likely to get updated.

What doesn't belong in the vault

The instinct when an agent is doing the writing is to let it document
everything, because it's free. But every line it writes is a line you have to
proofread and a line it has to read on every future run.

The thing to cut first is code detail. You don't need a note listing every
parameter on every method, or a walkthrough of what each function does line by
line. That information is already documented by the code itself.

Keep the vault at the level the code can't tell you. Why the retry logic backs
off the way it does. What the endpoints are actually doing at a high level. The
reasoning behind an architecture decision nobody wrote down at the time. That's
the stuff you can't reconstruct from source.

Two more things I've learned to leave out.

The first is the agent's own reasoning. When Claude works through a problem it'll
often narrate how it got there, what it ruled out, what it checked, and why it
landed where it did. That's useful to read in the moment, but it becomes noise
in a document.

The second is anything that has an authoritative source somewhere else — framework
docs, library references, the ticket describing the requirement, the Slack thread
where a decision got made. Copying those into the vault creates a second copy
that starts going stale immediately. Link to them instead.

The main idea is to keep your notes concise and at a high level to stop the AI
agent from hallucinating.

A decent test: if the information already lives somewhere authoritative — the
repo, the ticket, the docs — you don't need to duplicate it. Write down the part
that only exists in your head.

Summary

Documentation is hard to write and harder to keep current, and on a legacy
project with no maintainers that gap is where all your time goes. Pairing an
agent with Obsidian doesn't remove the work. You still proofread and keep things
in sync. What it changes is the kind of work. Instead of scanning your notes to
find information, you're scanning them to verify it, and that's a much
simpler job.

Let me know how it works for you.

a small book. It becomes too dense for a human to actually read. The more text
the agent has to go through, the more likely it is to hallucinate something that
isn't in there.

sentences.en: Agents write far too much.
sentences.zh: 代理人写得太多了。

sentences.en: Ask for documentation on a service and you'll get a small book.
sentences.zh: 询问有关服务的文档，您会得到一本小书。

sentences.en: It becomes too dense for a human to actually read.
sentences.zh: 它变得过于密集，以至于人类无法真正阅读。

sentences.en: The more text the agent has to go through, the more likely it is to hallucinate something that isn't in there.
sentences.zh: 智能体必须查看的文本越多，就越有可能产生其中不存在的幻觉。

blocks.html_en:
The fix is the most important habit when working with AI agents: proofread what
the agent wrote before you save it. It's tempting to trust Claude to write notes
and then never look at them, but a proofreading pass lets you cut the sections
you'll never need. Every paragraph you delete now is context the agent doesn't
have to process later.

sentences.en: The fix is the most important habit when working with AI agents: proofread what the agent wrote before you save it.
sentences.zh: 修复是使用人工智能代理时最重要的习惯：在保存之前校对代理所写的内容。

sentences.en: It's tempting to trust Claude to write notes and then never look at them, but a proofreading pass lets you cut the sections you'll never need.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易相信克劳德会写笔记，然后永远不看它们，但校对通过可以让你删除你永远不需要的部分。

sentences.en: Every paragraph you delete now is context the agent doesn't have to process later.
sentences.zh: 您现在删除的每个段落都是代理稍后不必处理的上下文。

blocks.html_en:
Notes drift out of sync. New information surfaces in conversation and never
makes it into the vault, so the next time you read the note it's wrong. Keeping
notes short is what makes them maintainable. If you can scan the section headers
of a note in ten seconds, you'll actually update it. Long notes are far less
likely to get updated.

sentences.en: Notes drift out of sync.
sentences.zh: 笔记变得不同步。

sentences.en: New information surfaces in conversation and never makes it into the vault, so the next time you read the note it's wrong.
sentences.zh: 新信息会在对话中出现，但永远不会进入保险库，因此下次您阅读该注释时，它是错误的。

sentences.en: Keeping notes short is what makes them maintainable.
sentences.zh: 保持笔记简短是它们易于维护的原因。

sentences.en: If you can scan the section headers of a note in ten seconds, you'll actually update it.
sentences.zh: 如果你能在十秒内浏览完笔记的章节标题，你就真的可以更新它了。

sentences.en: Long notes are far less likely to get updated.
sentences.zh: 长笔记更新的可能性要小得多。

blocks.html_en: What doesn't belong in the vault

sentences.en: What doesn't belong in the vault
sentences.zh: 什么不属于保险库

blocks.html_en:
The instinct when an agent is doing the writing is to let it document
everything, because it's free. But every line it writes is a line you have to
proofread and a line it has to read on every future run.

sentences.en: The instinct when an agent is doing the writing is to let it document everything, because it's free.
sentences.zh: 当代理进行写作时，本能是让它记录一切，因为它是免费的。

sentences.en: But every line it writes is a line you have to proofread and a line it has to read on every future run.
sentences.zh: 但它写入的每一行都是您必须校对的行，也是它在以后每次运行时都必须读取的行。

blocks.html_en:
The thing to cut first is code detail. You don't need a note listing every
parameter on every method, or a walkthrough of what each function does line by
line. That information is already documented by the code itself.

sentences.en: The thing to cut first is code detail.
sentences.zh: 首先要削减的是代码细节。

sentences.en: You don't need a note listing every parameter on every method, or a walkthrough of what each function does line by line.
sentences.zh: 您不需要列出每个方法的每个参数的注释，也不需要逐行演练每个函数的作用。

sentences.en: That information is already documented by the code itself.
sentences.zh: 该信息已由代码本身记录。

blocks.html_en:
Keep the vault at the level the code can't tell you. Why the retry logic backs
off the way it does. What the endpoints are actually doing at a high level. The
reasoning behind an architecture decision nobody wrote down at the time. That's
the stuff you can't reconstruct from source.

sentences.en: Keep the vault at the level the code can't tell you.
sentences.zh: 将保管库保持在代码无法告诉您的级别。

sentences.en: Why the retry logic backs off the way it does.
sentences.zh: 为什么重试逻辑会按原样退出。

sentences.en: What the endpoints are actually doing at a high level.
sentences.zh: 端点实际上在高层做什么。

sentences.en: The reasoning behind an architecture decision nobody wrote down at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时没有人写下架构决策背后的推理。

sentences.en: That's the stuff you can't reconstruct from source.
sentences.zh: 这是你无法从源头重建的东西。

blocks.html_en: Two more things I've learned to leave out.

sentences.en: Two more things I've learned to leave out.
sentences.zh: 我还学会了忽略另外两件事。

blocks.html_en:
The first is the agent's own reasoning. When Claude works through a problem it'll
often narrate how it got there, what it ruled out, what it checked, and why it
landed where it did. That's useful to read in the moment, but it becomes noise
in a document.

sentences.en: The first is the agent's own reasoning.
sentences.zh: 首先是代理人自身的推理。

sentences.en: When Claude works through a problem it'll often narrate how it got there, what it ruled out, what it checked, and why it landed where it did.
sentences.zh: 当克劳德解决一个问题时，他经常会讲述它是如何到达那里的，它排除了什么，它检查了什么，以及为什么它会出现在这个地方。

sentences.en: That's useful to read in the moment, but it becomes noise in a document.
sentences.zh: 这对于当下阅读很有用，但在文档中却变成了噪音。

blocks.html_en:
The second is anything that has an authoritative source somewhere else — framework
docs, library references, the ticket describing the requirement, the Slack thread
where a decision got made. Copying those into the vault creates a second copy
that starts going stale immediately. Link to them instead.

sentences.en: The second is anything that has an authoritative source somewhere else — framework docs, library references, the ticket describing the requirement, the Slack thread where a decision got made.
sentences.zh: 第二个是任何在其他地方有权威来源的东西——框架文档、库参考、描述需求的票证、做出决定的 Slack 线程。

sentences.en: Copying those into the vault creates a second copy that starts going stale immediately.
sentences.zh: 将它们复制到保管库中会创建第二个副本，该副本立即开始失效。

sentences.en: Link to them instead.
sentences.zh: 而是链接到它们。

blocks.html_en:
The main idea is to keep your notes concise and at a high level to stop the AI
agent from hallucinating.

sentences.en: The main idea is to keep your notes concise and at a high level to stop the AI agent from hallucinating.
sentences.zh: 主要思想是让你的笔记保持简洁和高水平，以防止人工智能代理产生幻觉。

blocks.html_en:
A decent test: if the information already lives somewhere authoritative — the
repo, the ticket, the docs — you don't need to duplicate it. Write down the part
that only exists in your head.

sentences.en: A decent test: if the information already lives somewhere authoritative — the repo, the ticket, the docs — you don't need to duplicate it.
sentences.zh: 一个不错的测试：如果信息已经存在于权威的地方 - 存储库、票据、文档 - 你不需要复制它。

sentences.en: Write down the part that only exists in your head.
sentences.zh: 写下只存在于你脑海中的部分。

blocks.html_en: Summary

sentences.en: Summary
sentences.zh: 概括

blocks.html_en:
Documentation is hard to write and harder to keep current, and on a legacy
project with no maintainers that gap is where all your time goes. Pairing an
agent with Obsidian doesn't remove the work. You still proofread and keep things
in sync. What it changes is the kind of work. Instead of scanning your notes to
find information, you're scanning them to verify it, and that's a much
simpler job.

sentences.en: Documentation is hard to write and harder to keep current, and on a legacy project with no maintainers that gap is where all your time goes.
sentences.zh: 文档很难编写，也很难保持最新状态，而在没有维护人员的遗留项目中，差距就是你所有时间都花在的地方。

sentences.en: Pairing an agent with Obsidian doesn't remove the work.
sentences.zh: 将代理与 Obsidian 配对并不会消除工作量。

sentences.en: You still proofread and keep things in sync.
sentences.zh: 您仍然会校对并使内容保持同步。

sentences.en: What it changes is the kind of work.
sentences.zh: 它改变的是工作的类型。

sentences.en: Instead of scanning your notes to find information, you're scanning them to verify it, and that's a much simpler job.
sentences.zh: 您无需扫描笔记来查找信息，而是扫描笔记来验证信息，这是一项简单得多的工作。

blocks.html_en: Let me know how it works for you.

sentences.en: Let me know how it works for you.
sentences.zh: 让我知道它对您有何作用。

content_html_zh:
背景

生活中有很多细节需要我们记住。 最近，我一直在开发一个遗留项目，该项目是几年前编写的，没有维护人员留下。 我必须不断地挖掘自己的数千行笔记才能记住应用程序的特定部分是如何工作的。 筛选笔记以找到一个细节需要时间，我宁愿花在架构和构建上。

人工智能代理改变了这一点。 它们使存储和检索您几天、几个月或几年前写下的信息变得更加容易。

什么是黑曜石

Obsidian 是一款笔记应用程序，它将所有内容存储为纯 Markdown 文件。 它可以让您以灵活的方式组织和构建笔记，并且由于文件在磁盘上是纯文本，因此任何可以读取目录的东西都可以读取您的笔记，包括人工智能代理。

对于项目，我使用 Obsidian 作为我的个人文档：系统如何工作、为什么做出决定、流程是什么。 将其视为第二大脑。 一切都生活在一处。

使其与代理一起工作的部分不是应用程序，而是链接。 Obsidian 允许您使用 [[注释名称]] 在注释之间创建双向链接。 这会将您的保管库从一堆文件转变为一个图表，您可以向代理提供单个入口点。

我如何构建我的文件

Obsidian 足够灵活，有十几种合理的方法来设置它。 这是我的，但您可以根据自己的风格进行调整。

我保留了两个文件夹。 MOC 代表内容地图，每个主题保存一个名为 <主题名称> - MOC 的文件。 永久笔记包含其他一切。 每次我创建与主题相关的注释时，我都会在两个方向上链接它：MOC 中的 [[<永久注释名称>]] 和注释中的 [[<主题名称> - MOC]]。

以下文件是示例：

vault/
├── MOC/
│   └── Legacy Payments API - MOC.md
└── Permanent Notes/
    ├── Payments API - Endpoints.md
    ├── Payments API - Webhook Retry Logic.md
    ├── Payments API - Settlement Flow.md
    └── Payments API - Architecture Decisions.md

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

MOC 本身也刻意保持精简：

# Legacy Payments API - MOC

Legacy service handling card settlement.

## Reference

- [[Payments API - Endpoints]]
- [[Payments API - Webhook Retry Logic]]

## Design

- [[Payments API - Settlement Flow]]
- [[Payments API - Architecture Decisions]]

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

这就是整个技巧。 您不必将代理指向一个文件夹并希望它读取正确的内容，而是将其指向一个文件，该文件准确地告诉它哪些注释重要以及它们之间的关系。 您可以控制上下文窗口，而不是让文件系统为您决定。

将您的代理连接到保管库

此处无需设置插件或集成。 由于黑曜石笔记只是磁盘上的降价文件，因此任何可以读取您的文件系统的代理都可以读取您的保管库。

我的工作流程很简单：我在库根打开 Claude，并告诉它读取特定的 MOC 文件。

Read MOC/Legacy Payments API - MOC.md and the notes it links to.

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

或者，如果您不想考虑从哪里启动，则可以直接粘贴完整路径。

在根目录而不是在 MOC/ 内部打开的原因是链接指向外部。 您的 MOC 位于一个文件夹中，而它引用的每条注释都位于另一个文件夹中，因此作用域为 MOC/ 的代理必须到达其工作目录之外才能跟踪它们。 根据您的设置，这意味着每次都批准访问。

使用 MOC 代理

当我开始研究一个主题时，我首先创建 MOC 并为代理提供到达它的路径。

在遗留项目中，这意味着创建遗留支付 API - MOC，然后通过代码库要求 Claude 记录 API 端点、业务逻辑和流程 - 每一项都作为自己的永久注释登陆，并且每一项都链接回 MOC。 我也将我的架构文档写入了Vault，这样我就可以稍后参考它们，而不是从头开始重建推理。

一旦 MOC 有了一些实质内容，它就成为其他一切的切入点。 当我需要一个新功能的计划时，提示大致是：

阅读 MOC/Legacy Payments API - MOC.md 及其链接到的每条注释。 然后编写在结算流程中添加部分退款的实施计划。 标记现有注释中与更改相矛盾的任何内容。

高效工作的秘诀

在这变成有用的东西之前，我遇到了两件事。

代理人写得太多了。 询问有关服务的文档，您会得到一本小书。 它变得过于密集，以至于人类无法真正阅读。 智能体必须查看的文本越多，就越有可能产生其中不存在的幻觉。

修复是使用人工智能代理时最重要的习惯：在保存之前校对代理所写的内容。 人们很容易相信克劳德会写笔记，然后永远不看它们，但校对通过可以让你删除你永远不需要的部分。 您现在删除的每个段落都是代理稍后不必处理的上下文。

笔记变得不同步。 新信息会在对话中出现，但永远不会进入保险库，因此下次您阅读该注释时，它是错误的。 保持笔记简短是它们易于维护的原因。 如果你能在十秒内浏览完笔记的章节标题，你就真的可以更新它了。 长笔记更新的可能性要小得多。

什么不属于保险库

当代理进行写作时，本能是让它记录一切，因为它是免费的。 但它写入的每一行都是您必须校对的行，也是它在以后每次运行时都必须读取的行。

首先要削减的是代码细节。 您不需要列出每个方法的每个参数的注释，也不需要逐行演练每个函数的作用。 该信息已由代码本身记录。

将保管库保持在代码无法告诉您的级别。 为什么重试逻辑会按原样退出。 端点实际上在高层做什么。 当时没有人写下架构决策背后的推理。 这是你无法从源头重建的东西。

我还学会了忽略另外两件事。

首先是代理人自身的推理。 当克劳德解决一个问题时，他经常会讲述它是如何到达那里的，它排除了什么，它检查了什么，以及为什么它会出现在这个地方。 这对于当下阅读很有用，但在文档中却变成了噪音。

第二个是任何在其他地方有权威来源的东西——框架文档、库参考、描述需求的票证、做出决定的 Slack 线程。 将它们复制到保管库中会创建第二个副本，该副本立即开始失效。 而是链接到它们。

主要思想是让你的笔记保持简洁和高水平，以防止人工智能代理产生幻觉。

一个不错的测试：如果信息已经存在于权威的地方 - 存储库、票据、文档 - 你不需要复制它。 写下只存在于你脑海中的部分。

概括

文档很难编写，也很难保持最新状态，而在没有维护人员的遗留项目中，差距就是你所有时间都花在的地方。 将代理与 Obsidian 配对并不会消除工作量。 您仍然会校对并使内容保持同步。 它改变的是工作的类型。 您无需扫描笔记来查找信息，而是扫描笔记来验证信息，这是一项简单得多的工作。

让我知道它对您有何作用。
